scope: Four modern mercy collection illustrations, full-frame inspection and comparison with repository collection art plan.
globalConditions: All four are fictional present-day applications, not recorded parable events or documentary claims.
No visible Christ is present. No healing, ease or money-provision promise is made.
Actual alt replaces planned invisible backstory. Caption explicitly identifies interpretive imagined application.
Technical pass does not establish owner approval or final browser/crop acceptance.

entries.alt: Two adults kneel beside a park path and examine the ground, with one pointing near the pavement.
entries.caption: Two people give their attention to a search beside the path. This imagined present-day scene applies the care and persistence in the lost-coin parable: what matters to another person deserves our attention. It does not equate a person's worth with a possession.
entries.findings: Only two searching adults are visible, plus an unrelated distant passerby. Pointing finger, bracing palms, bent knees and expressions coherent; skin and fabric photographic. No hearing aid can be confidently identified.
conditions: Replace planned three-person/hearing-aid alt with actual two-person search description.
Do not claim a hearing aid has been found or is visible.

entries.alt: A woman points into an open binder held by a man wearing an instrument case at a music-room doorway.
entries.caption: At the music-room doorway, help with a rehearsal folder becomes a practical welcome. In this imagined example, a returning participant is given a way to rejoin. The joy of recovering the lost can inspire patient help with someone's next step, without assuming that absence itself means wrongdoing.
entries.findings: Two distinct adults with natural expressions. Binder support, pointing hand and visible fingers plausible. Instrument case, chairs and music stands establish setting. A prior absence cannot be inferred from pixels alone.
conditions: Identify return as the fictional scenario's premise, not a documented biography.
Do not imply that missing orchestra rehearsal equals sin.

entries.alt: A teenager gestures beside a bicycle with a bent front basket while an adult in an apron listens.
entries.caption: The damaged basket remains plainly in view as the teenager speaks. This imagined return of a borrowed bicycle connects repentance with honest acknowledgment and willingness to begin making things right. Like the returning son's confession, a truthful beginning matters before every consequence is resolved.
entries.findings: Basket visibly bent rather than neatly formed; bike supported by repair stand. Teen's hand on grip and open palm, adult's hand on hip and attentive posture credible. No obvious anatomy or material scene defect.
conditions: Borrowing, ownership and responsibility are fictional scenario context, not visible proof.
Do not state that a repair, forgiveness or reconciliation is already complete.

entries.alt: One woman points to a form on a clipboard while another writes beside the indicated row.
entries.caption: A record is being reviewed together. In this imagined example, a mistake is acknowledged and corrected instead of concealed. The two-sons parable directs attention toward changed action rather than reassuring words alone, inviting us to let an honest change of mind lead to practical follow-through.
entries.findings: Pointing fingertip, pen grip and paper contact coherent. Two faces natural, posture focused. Background volunteers ordinary atmospheric detail. Form text not readable enough to establish error or completion.
conditions: Caption error correction as the imagined application; alt describes only visible review and writing.
Do not quote or invent text on the form, personal data, or a completed correction.
